newsitem.title: UK: Greenpeace protesters served writs aboard BP rig.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace protesters served writs aboard BP rig.

text.p: Greenpeace protesters aboard a British Petroleum oil platform in the north Atlantic have been served with writs ordering them to end their occupation, a BP spokesman said on Thursday.
But the environmental group said it was unaware the writs had been served and was continuing its protest.

Writs were served on Wednesday Scottish legal officers to three protesters in a survival capsule strapped to the Stena Dee platform and the masters of two Greenpeace vessels, the Greenpeace and the Rainbow C, the BP spokesman said.
"The Sheriff's officers went on board the rig and went down to the capsule and talked through the walls of the pod. They left the documents near the pod," he said.
"The writs have been served to the satisfaction of the Sheriff's Office...We are confident (the protesters) know they have been served," he added.
The documents stated that the protesters were unlawfully interfering with legitimate operations and they should remove themselves immediately.
But the three activists were still in place on Thursday and BP said it was seeking further legal advice.
"We are carrying on with the occupation," a Greenpeace spokeswoman said. "If the rig starts to move we will deploy swimmers to stop it."
Greenpeace protesters have been aboard the Stena Dee since Saturday in an attempt to prevent it reaching the new Foinaven oilfield as part of its worldwide campaign against climate change.
On Thursday morning the rig was drifting about five miles away from the field, about 65 miles northwest of the Orkney islands off the north Scottish coast.
